problem:
The entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & k\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{3}$ and $det(A)=1-2k.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}

feedback.problem:
The entry ${a}_{11}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{4}{5}.$ Find the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & k\end{aligned}| & =2|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|+0|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-k-6)-(0-3) \\  & =-2k-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{11}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{11}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{11} & =(-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =-k-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{11}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{11} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2k-9}\cdot (-k-6) \\  & =\frac{k+6}{2k+9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{11}^{′}=\frac{4}{5}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k+6}{2k+9} & =\frac{4}{5} \\ 5(k+6) & =4(2k+9) \\ 5k+30 & =8k+36 \\ 3k & =-6 \\ k & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
